external.label: Thurston WP (1997) Three-Dimensional Geometry and Topology, §2.3 Poincaré Disk. Princeton UP. Mathematical content CC0/PD — defines the Poincaré disk model, geodesics as arcs orthogonal to the boundary, isometries as Möbius transformations in PSL(2,R), and the {p,q} tessellation conditions. Related: Thurston (1982) Three-dimensional manifolds, Kleinian groups and hyperbolic geometry. Bulletin AMS 6:357–381.
external.author: William P. Thurston

external.label: Coxeter HSM (1954) Regular honeycombs in hyperbolic space. Proc. ICM Amsterdam 3:155–169. CC0/Public Domain — introduces the notation and enumeration of {p,q,r} and {p,q} hyperbolic tessellations, proves (p−2)(q−2)>4 for the hyperbolic case, gives circumradius and inradius formulas via Napier's rules for right spherical triangles (adapted to H²). Related: Coxeter (1956) On Laves' graph of girth ten; Coxeter-Dynkin diagrams for reflection groups.
external.author: H.S.M. Coxeter

external.label: NumPy Developers (2020) Array programming with NumPy. Nature 585:357–362. BSD-3-Clause — https://numpy.org — complex-number array arithmetic for Möbius transformations; np.conj, np.angle, np.exp for the three-step reflection; math.atanh for hyperbolic distance. Related: https://github.com/numpy/numpy.
